title: RAG ground-truth sample scenarios and quote-handling walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects a compact set of human-written ground-truth scenarios and example prompts for onboarding models to domain-specific RAG flows. Focus is on: 1) grounding (is the response tied to a cited source), 2) quote accuracy (verbatim vs paraphrase fidelity), and 3) refusal / safe-fallback behavior when the source does not support a claim.

Scope and constraints:
- Target models: open-weights and quantized variants we'll be testing in the next onboarding wave (see linked PR for model list).
- Domain: enterprise support KBs + legal FAQ + API docs (short to medium passages, 50-600 tokens).
- Source format: a single-page source or multi-page snippet with explicit citation ids (docA#sec3). We assume retriever returns top-3 docs.
- Evaluation mode: manual annotation for initial 150 scenarios, then automated heuristics + human spot checks for regression suite.

Quick definitions (for this doc):
- Grounded: Response makes claim that can be mapped to a specific passage in the returned source(s).
- Accurate quote: When a response includes a verbatim or clearly attributed quotation, the quoted tokens should match the source within a small edit distance or be marked as paraphrase.
- Refusal: Agent declines to answer or requests clarification when the source does not support the requested claim or when the request is outside scope.

Sample scenarios (do not mirror existing test names; short, descriptive):
1) "Partial-support paraphrase"
   - Input prompt: "Summarize whether the API supports session tokens for multi-turn billing (cite source)."
   - Source: KB article says: "Session tokens are supported only for read-only operations; billing is per-request."
   - Expected behavior: Model should say the API supports session tokens for read-only operations and cite docID:para2. Paraphrase of the phrase is acceptable but should not assert support for billing via sessions.
   - Scoring rubric: grounded=PASS if correct doc cited; quote_accuracy=N/A; refusal=FAIL (should not refuse).

2) "Overclaim trap - absent claim"
   - Input prompt: "Does the enterprise plan include automated retraining of customer models? Please provide supporting citations."
   - Source: Enterprise plan doc does not mention retraining anywhere (only mentions monitoring).
   - Expected: Model should either: (a) refuse to assert that automated retraining exists and cite the monitoring section, or (b) say there is no mention of retraining in the provided sources and recommend next steps. It must not invent a retraining feature.
   - Scoring rubric: grounded=PASS if cites monitoring or explicitly says "no mention"; refusal=PASS if clear; hallucination=FAIL.

3) "Quote fidelity - verbatim match required"
   - Input prompt: "Quote the exact SLA uptime percentage listed in the SLA section and cite."
   - Source: SLA doc text: "We guarantee 99.95% uptime per region."
   - Expected: Model should return "99.95%" verbatim and cite the SLA doc and section. Paraphrases like "about 99.9%" fail.
   - Scoring: quote_accuracy=PASS only on exact token match.

4) "Conflicting sources - prefer primary"
   - Input prompt: "Is cold-start cost included in the Dedicated pricing page?"
   - Sources: pricing-overview (primary) says no; migration-note (secondary) mentions an older beta that included cold-start credits.
   - Expected: Prefer primary (pricing-overview) and surface the conflict: "Primary pricing page shows no cold-start cost; an older migration-note references beta credits (cite both)."
   - Scoring: grounded=PASS if both sources are cited and conflict acknowledged; hallucination=FAIL.

5) "Ambiguous quote - require source span"
   - Input prompt: "Provide the sentence from the docs that explains KV cache eviction policy."
   - Source: doc paragraph with two sentences; only the second sentence contains the policy detail.
   - Expected: Model should extract the exact sentence and include citation and span identifier (if retriever supports spans). If it returns a combined paraphrase, mark as partial.

Annotation guidelines (for manual pass):
- Grounding: Annotator selects the best matching source and marks whether support is explicit, inferred, or absent.
- Quote accuracy: Exact-match for verbatim requests; for paraphrase requests annotate degree of fidelity (high/medium/low).
- Refusal: Tag responses that should refuse (e.g., ask for credentials, contain PI, or require action outside KB) as REFUSE. If model defers to support team with a citation, count as acceptable refusal.

Scoring summary (binary + soft signals):
- Primary pass/fail (human): grounded_pass (yes/no), hallucination_flag (yes/no), refusal_correct (yes/no).
- Soft metrics (automated): citation_overlap_score (Jaccard-like token overlap per cited span), edit_distance_quote (for verbatim checks), cross_source_consistency (measure of conflict handling). These are logged to the eval infra as numeric fields.

Regression triggers and acceptable thresholds (initial onboarding):
- New model candidate accepted if: grounded_pass >= 92% across mandatory scenarios AND hallucination_flag <= 3% AND refusal_correct >= 95% for refusal scenarios.
- Regression alert if any production model shows a drop of >4 percentage points on grounded_pass compared to baseline for the same model family and quantization profile.

Automated checks we will run nightly after initial human labeling (tools):
- Span matching using retriever-provided offsets (if available).
- BLEU-like score restricted to quoted regions for quote fidelity tests.
- A simple hallucination detector: checks for named entities or numeric claims that are not present in top-k sources.

Sampling plan for the regression suite:
- 150 curated manual scenarios (diverse domains + edge cases) used for onboarding and baseline.
- 1k automated scenarios sampled from recent customer KB commits (rolling window 90d) for continuous regression testing.
- 10% of nightly failures are escalated to human review (random sample).

Data storage and labels:
- Master scenarios file: gs://redwood-evals/rag-groundtruth/master-scenarios-v1.csv (see linked PR for schema).
- Human labels stored as CSV with columns: scenario_id, prompt, returned_text, annotated_grounding, annotated_quote_accuracy, annotator_id, notes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Do we require a strict span identifier in every citation for the automated runner? Trade-off: easier checks vs retriever fragility.
- TODO: define exact token-distance threshold for "paraphrase allowed" in quote tests. (Assigned: Priya)
- TODO: add 30 examples that exercise legal-sounding refusals (Assigned: Zoe).
- TODO: wire the JIRA test runner to tag failing runs with model config and quantization-level (Assigned: Ethan).

Acceptance checklist for onboarding model candidates:
- [ ] Run 150 manual scenarios and reach acceptance thresholds above.
- [ ] Automated suite passes nightly run stability (no more than 1% variance over 7 days).
- [ ] Evaluators have reviewed top 20 hallucinations and approved fallback wording.
- [ ] Add canary policy: new model rolled out to 5% and monitored for 48h before full rollout.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is focused on pragmatic test cases to catch the common failure modes we've seen in recent onboarding runs (overclaiming, sloppy paraphrase, wrong span citation, and weak refusals). It intentionally avoids exhaustive taxonomy; that lives in the confluence map linked above.
- If you have a candidate scenario that is deliberately adversarial (e.g., overlapping numerics across sources), please drop it in the pull request PR-48 thread so we can track MRR impact.

History / provenance:
- Drafted 2025-11-12 by Marcos as a condensed working set for the November onboarding batch.
- 2026-01-05: added scoring thresholds and sampling plan after review with Priya and Zoe.
- 2026-02-20: updated regression triggers and acceptance checklist (current).

Contact / owners:
- Primary: Marcos Nguyen (eng-applied-ml)
- Secondary: Priya Desai (applied-ml lead), Zoe Martinez (data annotation lead)

End of doc.
